source.title: Omnigrok: Grokking Beyond Algorithmic Data
source.authors: Zi-Ming Liu; Eric J. Michaud; Max Tegmark

record.tranche_reason: The study measures grokking and its dependence on initialization, weight norm, weight decay, and data size using loss-landscape analysis and experiments, rather than reproducing the original study's exact method.
record.gate_note: Rows record the study's own experiments and measurements bearing on delayed generalization, its control through training choices, and data-size effects. Results cited from Power et al., Liu et al., and Nanda et al. are not recorded as study results.
record.test_reason: The study runs its own training experiments on delayed generalization. It covers modular addition, a teacher-student MLP, MNIST, IMDb and QM9, varying initialization scale, weight decay, data size and a weight-norm constraint, and adds reduced loss-landscape analysis. It is a different method aimed at the same question, and it is not one of the original sources.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors attribute grokking to a mismatch between training (L-shaped) and test (U-shaped) reduced losses against weight norm, with regularization slowly pulling large-norm overfit solutions to a Goldilocks norm. They induce grokking on MNIST, IMDb and QM9 only in a non-standard setup (large init, small data), where it is weaker. They eliminate it on modular addition by constraining weight norm, and attribute its dramatic algorithmic form to reliance on representation learning. They report no clear grokking in LLMs.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses reduced loss-landscape analysis and experiments across a toy teacher-student task, modular addition, MNIST, IMDb, and QM9. It varies initialization scale, weight decay, data size, and weight-norm constraints rather than reproducing the original study's exact experimental recipe.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcome varies with initialization scale, weight decay, training-set size, and whether weight norm is constrained. The reported weight-decay relationship has exceptions at very high and very low decay on MNIST.

fits_no_version.finding: Grokking is dramatic when test performance depends strongly on the learned representation (algorithmic addition), and absent when it depends weakly (full MNIST representation landscape, Fig 8).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The size of the grokking delay depends on how much generalization requires learning a representation from scratch.

fits_no_version.finding: On modular addition, weight norm peaks during overfitting, then falls below its initialization norm as the model generalizes (Fig 7a).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Generalization in grokking coincides with weight norm decreasing toward a Goldilocks radius.

record.problems: Some central landscape and trajectory explanations are reduced analyses or illustrative paths, and the paper acknowledges that reduced trajectories may deviate from full trajectories. Several plotted outcomes have no numerical uncertainty reported. The algorithmic training-size comparison is contour-based rather than a reported sweep of full training runs.
record.rows_left_out: The remaining reduced landscapes and illustrative trajectory details are not separate training-accuracy or test-accuracy outcomes; cited results from other studies are excluded.

untested.parts: No measured sweep of grokking time against training-set size on an algorithmic task; the data-size dependence comes only from reduced-landscape contours.
Only MNIST, IMDb, QM9 and teacher-student regression are covered; no lazy-to-rich characterization beyond weight norm/initialization scale.
Whether a more efficient generalizing circuit is favoured over memorization is not measured; ungrokking below the critical size after generalization is not tested.
No circuit formation or progress-measure analysis.
No LLM experiments; the authors say they have not observed clear grokking in LLMs.
Not tested; slingshot (Thilak et al.) is cited only and not ruled out.

missing.what: Reduced landscapes showing that at large data size train and test losses share a U shape, so no LU mismatch and no grokking is possible (de-grokking with more data).
Teacher-student reduced train and test losses: L-shaped train and U-shaped test curves with a test minimum at α≈1.
Full-data MNIST landscape over representation messiness showing no train/test mismatch and no grokking.

record.verdict_notes: The reader labelled the standard-initialization controls (R13, R17, R19) as limits_scope for V3. They actually confirm V3's claim that initialization switches the delay on and off, so they are reclassified as supports. The data-size results on the toy addition model (R8–R11) are contour or landscape inferences on a decoder with an interpolated, frozen representation, not measured training runs. Researchers should weigh them accordingly.

versions.untested_parts: The study tests modular addition, but does not report a systematic training-set-size sweep of observed grokking times on that task; its reported size comparison is based on loss-landscape contours.

It discusses representation learning and presents a reduced trajectory account, but does not measure the formation of an identifiable generalizing circuit, removal of memorizing components, or continuous mechanistic progress measures anticipating an accuracy jump.
The non-algorithmic experiments use MNIST, IMDb, QM9, and a toy teacher-student regression task; they do not test every modality or training regime named in the version.
No LLM pretraining or fine-tuning experiment on realistic data is reported. The paper says it has not observed clear grokking signals for large language models.
The study tests weight-decay and data-size effects and discusses weight norm, but does not directly test whether a more efficient generalizing circuit is favoured over memorization.
It does not compare whether runs converge to the same identifiable algorithm across architectures or hyperparameters.
It does not control for or test adaptive-optimizer instabilities or floating-point limits in the softmax as causes of grokking.

rows.subject: 5-100-100-5 MLP teacher-student setup

rows.measure: Steps to reach 95% train and test accuracy, using the stated regression-error threshold

rows.subject: 1-layer transformer on modular addition (p = 113)
rows.operation_detail: Train with unconstrained optimization and standard initialization
rows.measure: Train and test accuracy over optimization steps
rows.value: The paper describes an initial overfitting period followed by generalization; weight norm peaks during overfitting and later drops below its initialization norm as the model generalizes
rows.note: The experiment uses the setup of Nanda et al. (2023); the cited study's results are not counted separately.

rows.subject: 1-layer transformer on modular addition (p = 113)
rows.operation_detail: Constrain model weight norm to remain constant during optimization
rows.measure: Train and test accuracy over optimization steps
rows.value: Train and test accuracy improve concurrently; the paper says this largely eliminates grokking
rows.note: The study presents this as a way to de-grok the algorithmic task.
rows.check: 'reversed' is wrong: concurrent train/test improvement is the absence of delay, not an opposite effect. The row bears on V3's claim that weight norm can switch grokking off, which it shows (Fig 7b). V1 makes no claim about norm-constrained training, so the V1 link is removed.

source_check.correct: State: absent for delayed generalization. Reduced initialization and constant-norm training at α=0.8 largely eliminate grokking; train and test accuracy improve concurrently. This successful off-switch supports V3.
source_check.locator_found: Figure 7b caption; Section 5.1, De-grokking by constraining weight norm; text lines 1441–1469.
source_check.problem: Concurrent learning indicates absence of the delay; support for the switching claim should be expressed by the verdict.
